candidates.attacker_control: `userIds` is fully attacker-controlled: DELETE /sys/user/deleteRecycleBin?userIds=... (@RequestParam) and PUT /sys/user/putRecycleBin with JSON body {"userIds": "..."} (SysUserController lines 1244 and 1226). Each comma-separated element is interpolated into the SQL; injecting a single quote and a comment (e.g. an id followed by `') OR 1=1 -- `) changes the WHERE clause. No SqlInjectionUtil/filterContent call exists on this path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that (a) the endpoint is not anon (ShiroConfig only opens /sys/user checkOnlyUser, register, phoneVerification, passwordChange), so a JWT is required; (b) no global SQLi/XSS filter or MyBatis interceptor sanitizes SQL - MybatisInterceptor only fills audit fields, no SQL rewrite; (c) other batch operations in the codebase use `#{...}`/removeByIds and the mapper author even comments 'SQL注入风险' on the neighboring updateNullByEmptyString (whose ${fieldName} is only ever called with hardcoded "email"/"phone"); (d) the values are wrapped in quotes but never escaped, which is the flaw; (e) role checks are disabled on this controller. Remaining uncertainty is runtime-only (no execution performed).
candidates.impact: Arbitrary SQL execution in the context of the application's DB account on the `sys_user` table. With `OR 1=1` (or equivalent) the DELETE becomes `DELETE FROM sys_user WHERE del_flag = 1 AND id IN ('x') OR 1=1`, removing every user row (full account wipe-out / denial of service), and the UPDATE sets del_flag=0 for all rows. Boolean/time-based predicates (e.g. SLEEP/IF forms) permit blind extraction of sensitive columns such as password hashes and salts for offline cracking. The operation runs inside @Transactional but succeeds for valid injected SQL.
candidates.prerequisites: A valid X-Access-Token (the endpoint is not in the Shiro anon list; it falls under the `/**` jwt chain). No administrator role is needed: the `//@RequiresRoles({"admin"})` line at SysUserController:1242 is commented out and there is no class-level authorization annotation. An ordinary/demo/self-registered account suffices. MySQL/PG-style single-statement injection only; no multi-statement support is required.
candidates.root_cause: Request-supplied user IDs are not validated or quote-escaped. SysUserController takes `userIds`, splits on "," and passes the raw List to the service. SysUserServiceImpl.revertLogicDeleted (line 462) and removeLogicDeleted (line 469) build a SQL fragment with String.format("'%s'", String.join("','", userIds)) and hand it to the mapper, where SysUserMapper.xml uses raw MyBatis substitution: `AND id IN (${userIds})` in revertLogicDeleted (line 144) and `AND id IN (${userIds})` in deleteLogicDeleted (line 149). Because a `'` inside any element is never escaped, it terminates the string literal and lets the attacker append arbitrary boolean/function expressions to the WHERE clause of the DELETE/UPDATE.
candidates.title: Authenticated SQL injection in /sys/user/deleteRecycleBin and /sys/user/putRecycleBin via unescaped userIds interpolation
candidates.trace: HTTP request (DELETE /sys/user/deleteRecycleBin?userIds=... | PUT /sys/user/putRecycleBin body) -> SysUserController.deleteRecycleBin / putRecycleBin -> Arrays.asList(userIds.split(",")) -> SysUserServiceImpl.removeLogicDeleted / revertLogicDeleted -> String.format("'%s'", String.join("','", userIds)) -> SysUserMapper.deleteLogicDeleted / revertLogicDeleted -> MyBatis XML `${userIds}` -> SQL text sent to `sys_user` DELETE / UPDATE. Because the interpolated value is only single-quoted, a `'` in the value escapes the literal.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. DB-specific parsing of the injected comment/quote was not executed; MySQL and PostgreSQL accept `-- ` while Oracle uses `--` - the payload is adaptable. The availability of default/demo credentials and the exact JWT/captcha flow were inferred from source (ShiroConfig, LoginController) and not exercised.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

coverage_summary: Source scope: 840 model-visible files (553 Java, plus resources/SQL/JS); 0 files excluded for size, sensitive names, or symlinks; binary-like files are skipped only when a NUL byte appears in the first 8 KiB. Relation index: complete (840/840 files indexed, 553 Java parsed, 0 parse errors, 0 missing files), but it provides only syntax-level containment/call/inheritance candidates with no control-flow, data-flow, or semantic resolution (13,304 unresolved calls), so every relation lead was re-verified in source text. I read and traced the base-core query/dict/security/shiro/sign/filter/config classes, the system module's user, dict, comment, upload, data-source, announcement, quartz and api controllers plus their service/mapper XML sinks, the CAS client path, the demo mock/online controllers, and the cloud gateway/xxl-job configuration. I did not exhaustively review all 840 files: vendor/static JS assets, the large SQL dumps, and many boilerplate CRUD controllers were only sampled.
limitations: No code was executed; the SQL injection is a source-level finding and was not runtime-confirmed.
Authentication requirements (JWT validity, captcha/login flow) were inferred from ShiroConfig/JwtFilter/LoginController source, not exercised.
DB-specific parsing of injected quotes/comments was not tested; impact (mass delete/restore, blind extraction) is a modeled consequence of the raw substitution.
The P1 index has no data-flow or reachability analysis; all navigation labels were treated as unverified and confirmed only by reading source.
Coverage was targeted rather than exhaustive for the many CRUD controllers and static/vendor assets in the 840-file snapshot.

summary: This snapshot is JeecgBoot 3.4.3 (Spring Boot 2.6.6, Shiro + JWT, MyBatis-Plus). It is a large multi-module Java project (840 source-tree files, 553 Java). Many previously reported SQL-injection holes already carry mid-2022 mitigations (SqlInjectionUtil filters, sign interceptor, bizPath checks, Freemarker SAFER_RESOLVER, JdbcSecurityUtil), so I focused on remaining raw-SQL sinks that still receive request data. The strongest single candidate is an authenticated SQL injection in the user recycle-bin delete/restore feature: controller-supplied `userIds` are split on commas, wrapped in single quotes by string formatting, and inserted through MyBatis `${userIds}` directly into a DELETE and an UPDATE on `sys_user`. A single quote in one element breaks out of the literal, and the controller-level `@RequiresRoles("admin")` is commented out, so any authenticated account can execute injected SQL (mass delete/restore of all users or blind extraction).
